accepted.question_text:
For the modified focusing nonlinear Schrodinger equation on R^d, with d = 2 in the no-group-velocity-dispersion case or d = 3 in the anomalous-group-velocity-dispersion case,

 i partial_t v + Delta v + (1 + f(epsilon^r |v|^2)) |v|^2 v = 0,

where f models high-intensity corrections such as a cubic-quintic or saturated nonlinearity, can one rigorously prove the oscillatory dynamics reported in experiments and numerics, in which a solution focuses, then defocuses, then refocuses, in an almost periodic or recurrent way rather than simply collapsing once?

evidence.quote: (51) i∂tv + ∆v + (1 + f(ε^r|v|^2))|v|^2v = 0, t > 0, x ∈ R^d, where the dimension is d = 2 in the case of no GVD, and d = 3 in the case of anomalous GVD.
Physical experiments suggest an oscillatory behavior of the solution which focuses, then defocuses, refocuses,... in an almost periodic fashion (see [3] and references therein).
Open Problem 1. Establish rigorously the "oscillatory" phenomenon of the solutions to (51) observed in physical experiments (see e.g. [3]).

accepted.question_text:
Fix d in {2, 3}, let v_0 in H^1(R^d) be initial data for the cubic focusing NLS that produce a finite-time blow-up solution v at time T > 0, and let v_epsilon be the solution of the regularized equation

 i partial_t v + Delta v + (1 + f(epsilon^r |v|^2)) |v|^2 v = 0

with the same initial data. What is the limiting behavior of v_epsilon(t) as epsilon tends to 0 for times t > T, that is, after the blow-up time of the unregularized cubic NLS has already passed?

evidence.quote: (51) i∂tv + ∆v + (1 + f(ε^r|v|^2))|v|^2v = 0, t > 0, x ∈ R^d, where the dimension is d = 2 in the case of no GVD, and d = 3 in the case of anomalous GVD.
An interesting question is the understanding of the limit of v_epsilon(t) as epsilon -> 0 for t > T .

Open Problem 2. Let v0 in H1(Rd), d = 2, 3 be leading to a finite time blow-up solution v at time T > 0 to the cubic NLS (1). Consider the solution v_epsilon of (51) with the same initial data v0. Describe the behavior of v_epsilon(t) as epsilon -> 0 for t > T .

accepted.question_text:
Consider the ionization-coupled variants of the focusing cubic NLS used for laser filamentation, namely the fixed-frame system

 i(partial_t + c_g partial_z)u + epsilon(Delta_perp + alpha_1 partial_z^2)u + epsilon(|u|^2 - rho)u = -i epsilon c(alpha_4 |u|^{2K-2}u + alpha_5 rho u),
 partial_t rho = epsilon alpha_4 |u|^{2K} + epsilon alpha_5 rho |u|^2,

and the moving-frame version

 i partial_tau v + (Delta_perp + alpha_1 partial_z^2)v + (|v|^2 - rho_tilde)v = -i c(alpha_4 |v|^{2K-2}v + alpha_5 rho_tilde v),
 -c_g partial_z rho_tilde = epsilon alpha_4 |v|^{2K} + epsilon alpha_5 rho_tilde |v|^2,

where the paper prescribes the boundary condition lim_{z -> +infinity} (nabla_perp)^l rho_tilde(tau, X_perp, z) = 0 for all l >= 0. Can one prove that solutions of these ionization models are global in dimensions 2 and 3, so that ionization really prevents finite-time collapse?

accepted.question_text:
For the modified focusing cubic NLS

 i P_2(epsilon nabla) partial_t v + Delta v + |v|^2 v = 0,

assume that the positive self-adjoint operator P_2(epsilon nabla) gives only partial off-axis regularization, meaning it controls derivatives only in some distinguished directions rather than the full H^1 norm. Can one develop both the local and the global well-posedness theory in that partial off-axis case, and in particular decide whether this partial off-axis dependence is enough to prevent finite-time breakdown of solutions that would blow up for the standard focusing cubic NLS?

evidence.quote: (60) iP2(ε∇)∂tv + ∆v + |v|^2v = 0, where d = 2 in the case of no GVD, and d = 3 in the case of anomalous GVD.

(66) (P2(ε∇)v, v) & ||v||^2_{L^2} + ε^2 Σ_{k=1}^j ||v_k · ∇v||^2_{L^2}, for vectors v_k in R^d, k = 1, . . . , j, where j = 1 if d = 2, and j = 1 or j = 2 if d = 3 so that the right-hand side of (66) does not control the full H^1 norm.
Now, it would be interesting to investigate whether a suitable well-posedness theory together with the conserved quantities given by the energy and (61) yield global existence.

Open Problem 4. Investigate both the local and global well-posedness for equation (60) in the case of partial off-axis dependence. In particular, does the modification of the focusing cubic NLS (1) by the addition of a partial off-axis dependence prevent the finite-time breakdown of the solutions?

accepted.question_text:
For the self-steepening model

 i partial_t v + Delta v + (1 + i epsilon alpha_3 . nabla)(|v|^2 v) = 0

in dimension 2 for no group velocity dispersion or dimension 3 for anomalous group velocity dispersion, how can the finite-time blow-up solutions behave? In particular, can one rigorously describe the blow-up scenarios, including whether solutions can develop the shock-like profiles that the paper associates with optical self-steepening?

evidence.quote: (68) i∂tv + ∆v + (1 + iεα3 · ∇)|v|^2v = 0, where d = 2 in the case of no GVD, and d = 3 in the case of anomalous GVD.
Thus, an interesting open problem would be to exhibit solutions of (68) for which the corresponding profile develops a shock.
Open Problem 5. Describe the blow-up scenarios for the finite time blow-up solutions to equation (68).

accepted.question_text:
For the hyperbolic or non-elliptic cubic NLS

 i partial_t v + (Delta_perp - partial_z^2)v + |v|^2 v = 0

in dimensions 2 and 3, can one prove that every H^1 solution is global, despite the lack of the standard elliptic structure of the usual focusing cubic NLS?

evidence.quote: Thus an interesting problem would be to prove that the cubic NLS equation (69) (i.e. in the case of normal GVD) does not have finite time blow up solutions, whether this is due to pulse splitting, or to some other phenomenon.
Open Problem 6. Prove that the solutions to equation (69) are global in dimension 2 and 3.

accepted.question_text:
For the hyperbolic cubic NLS

 i partial_t v + (Delta_perp - partial_z^2)v + |v|^2 v = 0,

can one rigorously prove and describe the pulse-splitting phenomenon seen in simulations, where a concentrating pulse reaches a threshold and then separates into lower-amplitude pulses moving apart instead of forming a singularity?

evidence.quote: In particular, the simulations exhibit a phenomenon called pulse splitting where the pulse focuses until it reaches a certain threshold. Once this threshold is attained, the pulse splits in two pulses of less amplitude moving away from each other.
Open Problem 7. Describe rigorously the phenomenon of pulse splitting for equation (69).

accepted.question_text:
When partial off-axis variation of the group velocity and longitudinal self-steepening are both present in the same direction, namely for

 i(1 - epsilon^2 partial_z^2) partial_t v + Delta v + (1 + i epsilon partial_z)(|v|^2 v) = 0,

do solutions still exhibit self-steepening, or does the off-axis regularization suppress or qualitatively change that shock-like steepening effect?

evidence.quote: Then, one may wonder whether the partial off-axis variation of the group velocity prevents the self-steepening from taking place.
Open Problem 8. Do the solutions to equation (72) exhibit the phenomenon of self-steepening?

accepted.question_text:
For the two-component complex vector version of the modified NLS model, where v is C^2-valued and satisfies

 i P_2(epsilon nabla) partial_tau v + (Delta_perp + alpha_1 partial_z^2)v + i alpha_2 v + (1/3)(1 + i epsilon alpha_3 . nabla)((v . v)v + 2|v|^2 v) = 0,

can one investigate the vectorial counterparts of the scalar open problems studied in the paper, including the analogues of the questions about global existence versus blow-up, pulse splitting, self-steepening, mixed effects, and long-time approximation of the underlying Maxwell equations?

accepted.question_text: The paper rigorously derives several NLS-type asymptotic models from Maxwell's equations and justifies them on times of order T/epsilon only while the approximating NLS-type solution stays bounded, which in the standard focusing case means times strictly before the focusing time T_foc. Can one rigorously justify at least one of these derived NLS-type models on a time interval [0, T/epsilon] with T greater than or equal to the focusing time T_foc, so that the approximation remains valid in the regime where the different models begin to differ in a physically meaningful way?

evidence.quote: It follows that all the NLS-type equations derived here are justified far enough from the focusing time.
Open Problem 10. Rigorously justify one of the NLS-type models derived here on a time scale [0, T /epsilon] with T >= Tfoc.
